turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Why does my son have a zero?
I appreciate you coming in with an open mind.
Don't manage me, Hale. I came in with a question, and you haven't answered it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
A lot of parents in your position would have gone straight to the principal. You didn't. That says a lot about you.
Flattery isn't an answer, Hale. I haven't ruled out the principal; I'm going up there when we're done unless you give me a reason not to. Who decided on the zero?
So I'd like to keep this between us and keep it friendly. Deal?
No deal. Nothing here is between us, and I'm writing down that you asked. What do you have on Owen's essay, Hale?
